facts.name: Production duration from a planner template row
facts.described_as: Crew-days to do a quantity of one finishing-trade work item at the planner template's rate: duration = quantity / rate per crew-day. The work item is one template row, named exactly as the row is (see the productivity.* knowledge entries for each row's unit and crew). The quantity's unit goes in quantity_unit; a quantity written with a unit of its own is taken in that unit. A quantity in another unit of the row's kind (sq ft for an m2 row) is converted into the row's unit and the conversion reported in unit_conversion; another kind is refused, naming both, and a quantity with no unit is asked for its unit. Unverified owner-supplied template: never a project figure.

inputs.name: work_item
inputs.label: planner template row (work item, as the row names it)

inputs.name: quantity_unit
inputs.label: unit the quantity is measured in

cites.credit: Production duration from a planner template row

hints.purpose: Crew-days for a quantity of one finishing-trade work item at a planner template row's rate. You name the row (the productivity.* knowledge entries list each row's unit, crew and what it does not cover); the calculator checks the quantity's unit against the row's.

not_to_be_confused_with.difference: productivity_benchmark only reads a row's rate; crew_days_from_rate_row also takes the quantity and its unit, checks the unit against the row and gives the crew-days.
productivity_manpower_duration takes a rate you already have (stated in the project's documents); crew_days_from_rate_row takes the template row's rate.
